chosen_property.label: hasLocation
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the geographical or physical place where something is situated or occurs.
chosen_property.justification: No suitable schema.org property found among candidates for a general location of an event.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: serviceLocation
candidates.comment: The physical place where a service can be accessed or obtained. Also called service access point, physical service location, service venue. Examples: `Bank Service Channel` serviceLocation `Bank Branch`, `Government Service Channel` serviceLocation `City Hall`, `Repair Service Channel` serviceLocation `Repair Shop`. Distinct from `serviceArea`, which is the broader geographic region.

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: itemLocation
candidates.comment: A physical location relation between an archive component and its current place, postal address, or textual description of location. Also called current location, item whereabouts, storage location, physical location. Examples: An archive component has an itemLocation of 'Shelf 3, Box 12'. An archive component has an itemLocation of 'Library Basement'. An archive component has an itemLocation of '123 Main St, Anytown'.

candidates.label: contentLocation
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, indicating the place depicted or described within its content. Also called "depicted location", "setting", "place of content". Examples: "Photograph contentLocation 'Eiffel Tower'", "Novel contentLocation 'London'".

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: jobLocation
candidates.comment: An employment location relation between a job posting and the primary geographic place where the work is performed. Also called work location, employment site, job site, place of work. Examples: A job posting has a jobLocation of 'New York City'. A job posting has a jobLocation of 'San Francisco Bay Area'. A job posting has a jobLocation of 'Remote'. Distinct from jobLocationType, which describes the *type* of location (e.g., 'TELECOMMUTE').

candidates.label: bodyLocation
candidates.comment: A textual description of the location in the body of an anatomical structure or for a medical procedure. Also called: anatomical site, body region, procedure location. Examples: "AnatomicalStructure 'Heart' bodyLocation 'Chest'", "MedicalProcedure 'Appendectomy' bodyLocation 'Abdomen'."

candidates.label: pickupLocation
candidates.comment: A spatial attribute indicating the place where a taxi will pick up a passenger or a rental car can be collected. Also called collection point, pick-up point, embarkation point. Examples: A taxi reservation has a pickup location of 'Grand Central Station'. A rental car reservation has a pickup location of 'Airport Terminal 1'. The ride-share booking has a pickup location at 'Home Address'.

candidates.label: isLocatedInSubcellularLocation
candidates.comment: A subcellular localization relation between a biochemical entity and its specific location within a cell. Also called found in subcellular location, localized to, present in subcellular compartment. Examples: A protein is isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'cytoplasm'. DNA is isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'nucleus'. Mitochondrial enzymes are isLocatedInSubcellularLocation 'mitochondrion'.

candidates.label: superEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: sportsEvent

candidates.label: subEvent

candidates.label: subEvents

Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: scheduledTime

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". candidates.label: doorTime

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: coverageEndTime

Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage end time "2024-11-06T04:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage end time "2023-07-15T19:30:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage end time "2023-10-27T17:00:00Z". candidates.label: observationDate

Examples: "A forum question's accepted answer is 'Use a screwdriver'.", "A quiz question's accepted answer is 'Option B'."

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: certificationStatus
candidates.comment: A status relation for a certification, indicating whether it is active or inactive. Also called "certificate status", "certification validity", "status of certification". Examples: "Product certification certificationStatus Active", "Company certification certificationStatus Inactive".

candidates.label: equal
candidates.comment: An equality relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject qualitative value is considered equal to the object qualitative value within a specific ordering context. Also called "is equivalent to", "is the same as", "matches". Examples: "Qualitative value 'Satisfactory' equal 'Acceptable'", "Qualitative value 'Medium' equal 'Average'", "Qualitative value 'High' equal 'Very Good'".

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: signDetected
candidates.comment: A medical sign or objective indicator identified through a medical test. Also called test finding, detected symptom, medical indicator. Examples: `Blood Test` signDetected `MedicalSign: Elevated White Blood Cell Count`, `X-Ray` signDetected `MedicalSign: Bone Fracture`, `Physical Exam` signDetected `MedicalSign: Swelling`. Distinct from `symptom`, which is a subjective experience.

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

candidates.label: travelBans
candidates.comment: A travel bans relation between a special announcement and information regarding restrictions on travel. Also called travel restrictions, ban on travel, travel advisories. Examples: "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://example.com/travel-restrictions'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'All international travel is suspended.'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://who.int/travel-guidance'".

candidates.label: publicTransportClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: A public transport closures information relation between a special announcement and details regarding public transport disruptions. Also called transport closure details, public transit alerts. Examples: "A special announcement includes public transport closures info about subway lines.", "An emergency alert provides public transport closures info for bus routes.", "A news update contains public transport closures info for train services."

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: legislationRepeals
candidates.comment: A repeal relation between two pieces of legislation, where one cancels or abrogates the other. Also called: cancels, abrogates, revokes. Examples: "New Act legislationRepeals Old Act", "Regulation X legislationRepeals Directive Y", "Law 123 legislationRepeals Statute 456".

candidates.label: ineligibleRegion
candidates.comment: A geographical exclusion relation between an action access specification, delivery charge specification, demand, media object, or offer, and the region where it is not valid or available. Also called restricted region, excluded region, unavailable in, not valid in. Examples: An offer has an ineligibleRegion of 'Alaska'. A delivery charge specification has an ineligibleRegion of 'Hawaii'. A media object has an ineligibleRegion of 'EU'. Distinct from eligibleRegion, which specifies where something *is* valid or available.

candidates.label: smokingAllowed
candidates.comment: An indicator of whether smoking is permitted within a specific place. Also called smoking policy, smoke-free status, smoking permitted. Examples: `Restaurant` smokingAllowed `false`, `Hotel Room` smokingAllowed `true`, `Public Park` smokingAllowed `false`.

candidates.label: itemCondition

candidates.label: startTime

Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". candidates.label: hasCredential

candidates.label: hasCertification

candidates.label: skills

candidates.label: employee

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: qualifications
candidates.comment: A qualification relation between a job posting or occupation and the specific credentials or skills required. Also called required skills, job requirements, eligibility criteria. candidates.label: hasPOS
candidates.comment: A point-of-sale relation between an organization or person and a place where they operate a point of sale. Also called operates POS, sales location, retail point. candidates.label: legalRepresentative

candidates.label: image

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. candidates.label: bankAccountType

candidates.label: encoding
candidates.comment: An encoding relation between a creative work and a media object that represents or contains it. Also called "represented by media", "media representation", "has media object". candidates.label: disambiguatingDescription
candidates.comment: A clarifying description relation between a thing and a short text used to distinguish it from similar items. Examples: "Apple" disambiguating description "The fruit, not the company.", "Mercury" disambiguating description "The planet, not the element.", "Jaguar" disambiguating description "The animal, not the car brand.". candidates.label: encodings
candidates.comment: An encodings relation between a creative work and the media objects that represent or contain it. Also called "represented by media objects", "has media representations", "media versions". Examples: "Movie 'The Matrix' encodings 'Matrix.mp4', 'Matrix.avi'", "Song 'Bohemian Rhapsody' encodings 'BohemianRhapsody.mp3', 'BohemianRhapsody.wav'", "Book '1984' encodings '1984.epub', '1984.pdf'". Distinct from encodesCreativeWork, which is the inverse relation (MediaObject -> CreativeWork).

candidates.label: representativeOfPage
candidates.comment: A representative of page relation indicating whether an image object accurately reflects the content of the web page it appears on. Also called page representative, content summary image. Examples: "A thumbnail image is representative of page 'true'.", "A decorative image is representative of page 'false'.", "A product photo is representative of page 'true'."

candidates.label: caption
candidates.comment: A descriptive text or media object providing a caption for an audio, image, or video object. Also called "description", "subtitle", "alt text". Examples: "Image object caption 'Sunset over the mountains'", "Video object caption 'English subtitles'", "Audio object caption 'Transcript of speech'".

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: sourcedFrom
candidates.comment: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: evidenceOrigin
candidates.comment: An evidence origin relation between a medical guideline and the source of data used to formulate it. Also called: data source, guideline source, origin of evidence. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" evidence origin "RCT", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" evidence origin "Consensus Opinion", "WHO Guideline for COVID-19" evidence origin "Observational Studies". Distinct from evidenceLevel, which is the strength of the evidence.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: originatesFrom
candidates.comment: A vessel from which a lymphatic structure originates or receives afferents. Also called arises from, derived from, source vessel. Examples: "Lymphatic Vessel A originatesFrom 'Capillary Bed X'", "Thoracic Duct originatesFrom 'Cisterna Chyli'", "Lymphatic Capillary originatesFrom 'Interstitial Fluid'". Distinct from runsTo, which describes the destination.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: dateline
candidates.comment: A textual origin relation between a news article and the brief text describing where and when the story was written or filed. Also called: news origin, article origin, reporting location. Examples: "News Report" dateline "BEIRUT, Lebanon, June 2.", "Article" dateline "Paris, France", "Dispatch" dateline "December 19, 2017 11:43AM Reporting from Washington". Distinct from locationCreated, which is a structured representation of the creation location.

candidates.label: shippingOrigin
candidates.comment: The geographical region or location from which a shipment originates. Also called shipment source, origin of delivery, dispatch location. Examples: `Offer Shipping Details` shippingOrigin `DefinedRegion: California`, `Shipping Conditions` shippingOrigin `DefinedRegion: Warehouse A`, `International Shipment` shippingOrigin `DefinedRegion: China`. Distinct from `shippingDestination`, which is where the shipment goes.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.comment: A creative work, such as an image, video, or audio clip, that is included or shared within a comment or social media posting. candidates.label: distribution

Also called "data download", "dataset version", "downloadable resource". Examples: "Dataset 'Census Data' distribution 'CSV file'", "Research data distribution 'Excel spreadsheet'", "Open data portal distribution 'API endpoint'".

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: itemShipped

Examples: A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'a book'. A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'clothing items'. A parcel delivery has an itemShipped of 'electronic device'.

candidates.label: healthPlanCostSharing

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: free
candidates.comment: A free relation indicating whether a publication event, item, or place is accessible without cost. Also called: no charge, complimentary, gratis. Examples: "Online Article Publication" free "true", "Concert Event" free "false", "Public Park Access" free "true".

candidates.label: partOfOrder
candidates.comment: A logistical relation between a parcel delivery and the larger order it fulfills. Also called fulfills, belongs to, is a shipment for, is included in. Examples: A package delivery is part of an online shopping order. A food delivery is part of a restaurant order. A furniture shipment is part of a home goods order.

candidates.label: colleagues

candidates.label: sourcedFrom
candidates.comment: An anatomical origin relation between a nerve and the brain structure from which its neurons originate. Also called "originates from", "nerve pathway source", "derived from brain structure". Examples: "The optic nerve is sourcedFrom the diencephalon", "Cranial nerve V is sourcedFrom the brainstem", "This nerve's neurons are sourcedFrom the spinal cord."

candidates.label: originatesFrom
candidates.comment: A vessel from which a lymphatic structure originates or receives afferents. Also called arises from, derived from, source vessel. Examples: "Lymphatic Vessel A originatesFrom 'Capillary Bed X'", "Thoracic Duct originatesFrom 'Cisterna Chyli'", "Lymphatic Capillary originatesFrom 'Interstitial Fluid'". Distinct from runsTo, which describes the destination.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: validFrom
candidates.comment: A valid from relation between a certification, demand, financial incentive, location feature specification, monetary amount, offer, opening hours specification, permit, or price specification and the date it becomes valid. Also called effective date, start date, activation date. Examples: "Offer validFrom '2023-11-01'", "Permit validFrom '2023-01-01T09:00:00'", "OpeningHoursSpecification validFrom '2024-01-01'". Distinct from validThrough or validUntil, which specify the end of validity.

candidates.label: ownedFrom
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.

candidates.label: availableFrom
candidates.comment: A date and time when an item is available for pickup from a store or locker. Also called: pickup start time, ready for collection. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableFrom '2023-10-27T10:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableFrom '2023-10-28'". Distinct from availableThrough, which specifies the end of pickup availability.

candidates.label: expectedArrivalFrom
candidates.comment: An expected arrival from relation between a parcel delivery and the earliest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: earliest arrival, minimum delivery date, estimated start arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival from "2023-10-26", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival from "2023-10-27T09:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival from "2023-11-01". Distinct from expectedArrivalUntil, which is the latest arrival date.

candidates.label: availableAtOrFrom
candidates.comment: A place from which an offer can be obtained. Also called: pickup location, sales point, distribution point. Examples: "Offer 'Groceries' availableAtOrFrom 'Supermarket A'", "Offer 'Concert Tickets' availableAtOrFrom 'Venue Box Office'."

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: broadcastFrequencyValue
candidates.comment: A number or quantitative value representing the frequency in MHz for a particular broadcast. Also called: frequency in MHz, broadcast megahertz. Examples: "BroadcastFrequencySpecification 'FM 98.1' broadcastFrequencyValue '98.1'", "BroadcastFrequencySpecification 'TV Channel 25' broadcastFrequencyValue '539'."

relations.embedding_query_text: wearing:

candidates.label: suggestedMeasurement
candidates.comment: A quantitative value representing a suggested range of body measurements for an intended audience or person, often for wearable products. Also called "size recommendation", "body measurement range", "fit guide", "sizing suggestion". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedMeasurement inseam 32-34 inches", "The size specification includes suggestedMeasurement height 170-190 cm", "This product is designed for a suggestedMeasurement chest 40-42 inches."

candidates.label: sizeGroup
candidates.comment: The classification or category of a product's size, often used in fashion to define target audiences. Also called size type, size segment, apparel size group. Examples: `Dress Size` sizeGroup `"Petite"`, `Jeans Size` sizeGroup `"Men's Big and Tall"`, `Children's Clothing` sizeGroup `"Toddler"`. Distinct from `sizeSystem`, which is the measurement system used.

candidates.label: pattern
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the visual or design pattern of a creative work or product. Also called design, motif, print, style. Examples: A dress has a pattern of 'polka dot'. A fabric has a pattern of 'striped'. A flag has a pattern of 'Canadian flag'.

candidates.label: suggestedGender
candidates.comment: An indication of the recommended gender for an intended person or audience. Also called "target gender", "audience gender", "gender recommendation". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedGender unisex", "The audience specification includes suggestedGender female", "This product is for suggestedGender male."

candidates.label: size
candidates.comment: The standardized dimensions or measurement of a product or creative work. Also called dimensions, measurement, product size, item size. Examples: `T-Shirt` size `"XL"`, `Book` size `SizeSpecification: 6x9 inches`, `Shoe` size `QuantitativeValue: 10 US`. Distinct from `width`, `height`, `depth`, `weight`, which are specific dimensions.

candidates.label: color
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a product, indicating its color. Also called "product color", "hue", "shade". Examples: "Car product color 'Red'", "Shirt product color 'Blue'". Distinct from colorSwatch, which provides an image of the color.

candidates.label: vehicleInteriorColor
candidates.comment: A vehicle interior color relation between a vehicle and the color or color combination of its interior. Also called interior color, cabin color, upholstery color. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleInteriorColor 'Black'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorColor 'Beige Leather'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorColor 'Grey Fabric'".

candidates.label: athlete
candidates.comment: A person who is a performing member of a sports team. Also called: player, team member, sportsman/sportswoman. Examples: "SportsTeam 'Lakers' athlete 'LeBron James'", "SportsTeam 'Red Sox' athlete 'Mookie Betts'", "SportsTeam 'National Team' athlete 'Megan Rapinoe'". Distinct from coach, which is a non-playing role.

candidates.label: gender
candidates.comment: A gender relation between a person or sports team and their gender identity or classification. Also called: sex, gender identity, team gender. Examples: "John Doe" gender "Male", "Jane Smith" gender "Female", "Mixed Doubles Team" gender "Mixed".

candidates.label: sport
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of sport associated with a sports event or organization. Also called "sport type", "athletic discipline", "game played". Examples: "The event's sport is Basketball", "The organization's sport is Soccer", "This competition features the sport of Gymnastics."

relations.embedding_query_text: causedBy:

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: musicBy
candidates.comment: A composer or music group responsible for the soundtrack of a creative work. Also called soundtrack by, composer of, musical score by. Examples: "Movie X musicBy 'John Williams'", "TV Series Y musicBy 'Ramin Djawadi'", "Video Game Z musicBy 'Koji Kondo'". Distinct from composer, which is for the composer of a MusicComposition.

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: reviewedBy
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for reviewing the content of a webpage for accuracy or completeness. Also called content reviewer, page editor, accuracy checker. Examples: `Medical Information Page` reviewedBy `Dr. Jane Doe`, `News Article` reviewedBy `Fact-Checking Organization`, `Research Paper` reviewedBy `Peer Review Board`. Distinct from `author`, which indicates who created the content, not who reviewed it.

candidates.label: readBy
candidates.comment: A narration relation between an audiobook and the person who performs the reading. Also called narrated by, performed by, voiced by. Examples: "The audiobook 'Harry Potter' is read by 'Stephen Fry'.", "An autobiography audiobook is read by 'the author'.", "A classic novel audiobook is read by 'a professional narrator'."

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

relations.embedding_query_text: hasURL:

candidates.label: installUrl
candidates.comment: A download location relation between a software application and the URL from which it can be installed. Also called download URL, installation link, app download link. Examples: A software application has an installUrl of 'https://example.com/app/download'. A mobile game has an installUrl of 'https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.game'. A desktop utility has an installUrl of 'https://software.org/installer.exe'. Distinct from url, which is the general URL for the item, not specifically for installation.

candidates.label: isBasedOnUrl
candidates.comment: A source URL relation between a creative work and a specific URL that served as a resource for its creation. Also called source URL, derived from URL, based on URL, reference URL. Examples: A research paper has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://arxiv.org/abs/1234.5678'. A blog post has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://example.com/original-article'. A web page has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://old-version.com/page'. Distinct from isBasedOn, which can refer to any CreativeWork or Product, not just a URL.

candidates.label: targetUrl
candidates.comment: A URL identifying a node within an established educational framework. Also called "framework node URL", "educational standard URL", "learning objective URL". Examples: "The alignment object has targetUrl 'http://example.com/algebra-standard'", "The educational framework node's targetUrl points to its definition", "This targetUrl links to a specific competency."

candidates.label: mobileUrl
candidates.comment: A mobile URL relation between an offer or product and a dedicated URL for its mobile site. Also called: mobile link, mobile website, responsive URL. Examples: "Product Offer mobileUrl 'https://m.example.com/product1'", "Service Listing mobileUrl 'https://mobile.service.com'", "E-commerce Product mobileUrl 'https://example.com/mobile/item123'". Distinct from url, which is a general URL and ideally should be responsive for all devices.

candidates.label: contentUrl
candidates.comment: A location relation for a media object, providing the URL to its actual bytes or file. Also called "media URL", "file URL", "download link". Examples: "Image object contentUrl 'https://example.com/image.jpg'", "Video object contentUrl 'https://example.com/video.mp4'".

candidates.label: downloadUrl
candidates.comment: A download URL relation between a software application and the URL to download its binary file. Also called "software download link", "binary download", "installer URL". Examples: "Software application 'Image Editor' downloadUrl 'example.com/editor.exe'", "Mobile app downloadUrl 'appstore.com/app.apk'", "Operating system downloadUrl 'os.example.com/iso'".

candidates.label: paymentUrl
candidates.comment: A linking attribute providing the URL where payment for an order can be submitted. Also called payment link, checkout URL, pay now link. Examples: An order has a payment URL 'https://example.com/pay/123'. The invoice includes a payment URL 'https://secure.payment.com/invoice/XYZ'. The subscription has a payment URL for renewal.

candidates.label: serviceUrl
candidates.comment: The URL of the website used to access a service. Also called service website, online service portal, service access URL. Examples: `Online Banking Channel` serviceUrl `URL: bank.com/online`, `Government Portal` serviceUrl `URL: gov.agency/services`, `E-commerce Service` serviceUrl `URL: shop.com/support`. Distinct from `url`, which is a general URL for an entity.

candidates.label: embedUrl
candidates.comment: An embed URL relation between a media object and the URL pointing to a player for that media. Also called "player URL", "embed link", "streaming URL". Examples: "Video mediaObject embedUrl 'youtube.com/embed/videoid'", "Audio mediaObject embedUrl 'soundcloud.com/player/trackid'", "Interactive content embedUrl 'example.com/interactive/player'". Distinct from contentUrl, which is the direct URL to the media file itself.

candidates.label: trackingUrl
candidates.comment: A tracking URL relation between a parcel delivery and the web address for monitoring its status. Also called shipment tracking link, parcel status URL, delivery tracking page. Examples: "ParcelDelivery trackingUrl 'https://example.com/track/12345'", "ParcelDelivery trackingUrl 'https://shipper.com/status?id=ABCDE'", "ParcelDelivery trackingUrl 'https://delivery.com/track/FGHIJ'".

relations.embedding_query_text: hasPublicationDate:

candidates.label: sdDatePublished
candidates.comment: The date when the structured data associated with a creative work was generated or published. Also called structured data publication date, metadata publish date, data generation date. Examples: `Article JSON-LD` sdDatePublished `2023-10-26`, `Recipe Structured Data` sdDatePublished `2023-09-15`, `Event Markup` sdDatePublished `2023-08-01`. Distinct from `datePublished`, which is the publication date of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: datePublished
candidates.comment: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

candidates.label: hasCourseInstance
candidates.comment: A course offering relation between a course and a specific instance of that course. Also called course offering, instance of course, course session. Examples: "A calculus course has a course instance for Fall 2023.", "The online course has a course instance for self-paced study.", "A cooking class has a course instance on Tuesdays at 6 PM."

candidates.label: hasAdultConsideration
candidates.comment: An adult suitability relation between an offer or product and its intended audience or content rating. Also called adult-oriented, age-restricted, mature content, for adults only. Examples: "An offer has adult consideration for explicit content.", "A product is tagged with adult consideration.", "This item has adult consideration due to its theme."

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: hasDigitalDocumentPermission
candidates.comment: A document permission relation between a digital document and an associated access permission. Also called document access, permission for document, document rights. Examples: "A digital document has a digital document permission to read.", "The file has a digital document permission for editing.", "This document has digital document permissions for public viewing."

candidates.label: hasDeliveryMethod
candidates.comment: A delivery method relation between a delivery event or parcel delivery and the method used for its delivery. Also called delivery via, shipping method, method of delivery. Examples: "A parcel delivery has a delivery method of 'express shipping'.", "The delivery event has a delivery method of 'pickup'.", "The order uses a delivery method of 'standard mail'."

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: datePosted
candidates.comment: A temporal publication relation between a CDCPMD record, job posting, real estate listing, or special announcement and its online publication date. Also called: posting date, publication date, listing date. Examples: "Job Opening" date posted "2023-10-25", "Apartment for Rent" date posted "2023-10-20", "Public Health Alert" date posted "2023-03-01T09:00:00Z". Distinct from datePublished, which is a more general property for first publication.

candidates.label: hasOfferCatalog
candidates.comment: An offer catalog relation between an organization, person, or service and an associated offer catalog. Also called offers catalog, catalog of offers, product catalog. Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."
